Motivation of this package

Source: vignettes/articles/motivation.Rmd
motivation.Rmd

Old format of Fude Polygon data

The Fude Polygon data published by MAFF on https://open.fude.maff.go.jp for the years 2021 and 2022 is in GeoJSON format. These datasets include local government codes but lack the key column, which identifies geographical locations such as municipalities or communities. Relying solely on the 6-digit local government codes (the local_government_cd column) can be confusing, as most users are not familiar with them. Therefore, this package aims to enhance user-friendliness by converting these numeric codes into readable Japanese geographical names.

library(fude)

d0 <- read_fude("~/2022_38.zip", quiet = TRUE)
names(d0)
##  [1] "2022_382019" "2022_382027" "2022_382035" "2022_382043" "2022_382051"
##  [6] "2022_382060" "2022_382078" "2022_382108" "2022_382132" "2022_382141"
## [11] "2022_382159" "2022_383562" "2022_383864" "2022_384011" "2022_384020"
## [16] "2022_384224" "2022_384429" "2022_384844" "2022_384887" "2022_385069"
names(d0[[1]])
##  [1] "polygon_uuid"           "land_type"              "issue_year"            
##  [4] "edit_year"              "history"                "last_polygon_uuid"     
##  [7] "prev_last_polygon_uuid" "local_government_cd"    "point_lng"             
## [10] "point_lat"              "geometry"

Rename the local government code

Note: This feature is available only for data obtained from GeoJSON.

You can convert local government codes into Japanese municipality names for easier data management.

d1 <- rename_fude(d0)
names(d1)
##  [1] "2022_松山市"     "2022_今治市"     "2022_宇和島市"   "2022_八幡浜市"  
##  [5] "2022_新居浜市"   "2022_西条市"     "2022_大洲市"     "2022_伊予市"    
##  [9] "2022_四国中央市" "2022_西予市"     "2022_東温市"     "2022_上島町"    
## [13] "2022_久万高原町" "2022_松前町"     "2022_砥部町"     "2022_内子町"    
## [17] "2022_伊方町"     "2022_松野町"     "2022_鬼北町"     "2022_愛南町"

You can also rename the columns to Romaji instead of Japanese.

d2 <- d0 |>
  rename_fude(suffix = TRUE, romaji = "title", quiet = FALSE)
## 2022_382019 -> 2022_Matsuyama-shi

New format of Fude Polygon data

Since 2024, the Fude Polygon data published by MAFF https://www.maff.go.jp/j/tokei/census/shuraku_data/2025/mb/ is provided in FlatGeobuf format. This new format includes a key column that identifies municipalities and communities. However, it does not include the corresponding Japanese geographical names. Because the key is merely a 10-digit number, users cannot intuitively identify locations without mapping them to proper Japanese names.

dn <- read_fude("~/MB0001_2026_2025_38.zip.001", quiet = TRUE)
names(dn)
## [1] "MB0001_2026_2025_38"
names(dn[[1]])
## [1] "polygon_uuid" "land_type"    "issue_year"   "point_lng"    "point_lat"   
## [6] "key"          "geometry"

Combination with agricultural community boundaries

Combining Fude Polygons with agricultural community boundary data provides deeper geographical insights and makes the data much easier to work with.

b <- get_boundary(d0, path = "~", quiet = TRUE)
b

db <- d0 |>
  lapply(sf::st_transform, crs = sf::st_crs(b[[1]])) |>
  combine_fude(b, city = "松山市", rcom = "由良|北浦|鷲ケ巣|門田|馬磯|泊|御手洗|船越")
db
